content.comment_body: Hello, When using the [company_name] selection tool to set up a new project that includes [product_name], it seems that when configuring the maximum number of digital inputs and outputs, the settings shown by the tool do not count the digital I/O of the [product_name] base module in the total limits. Please refer to the attached image. Is this expected? To achieve the maximum of 24 digital inputs and 20 digital outputs supported by [product_name], is the entered configuration correct?

The details in the [company_name] selection tool consider only the inputs and outputs on the base module itself. For instance, a [product_name] base module with article number [article_no] offers 8 digital inputs and 4 digital outputs. However, with suitable expansion modules, the system can provide: - 24 digital inputs - 20 digital outputs - 8 analog inputs - 8 analog outputs If multiple [product_name] modules (with article number [article_no]) are networked, even more inputs and outputs can be managed using expansion modules.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about how the [company_name] selection tool calculates and displays total I/O for [product_name] systems. The main confusion is whether the digital inputs and outputs of the base module are included in the overall limits or only expansion module I/O is counted. The tool’s interface and explanations contribute to misinterpretations concerning achievable hardware configurations and system limits.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [company_name] selection tool to transparently show the total number of digital inputs and outputs, including both the base module and expansions. They seek confirmation that their configuration truly reaches the maximum supported capacity for their [product_name] setup.
